Homage

OM-ij (or hom-AHZH) — to 'pay homage' is to publicly honor someone, the way a knight once honored a lord. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Homage is special honor or respect shown publicly.

The retiring coach's former players returned from across the country to pay homage to him at his final game.

Worked Example

A young chef opens her own restaurant and names her signature dish after the grandmother who taught her to cook, serving it exactly the way her grandmother did every Sunday, right down to the same handwritten recipe card on the wall.

Publicly honoring someone's memory or legacy through a deliberate tribute is exactly what paying homage means. Unlike 'imitation,' which can be careless copying, homage is a respectful, intentional tribute.

How Strong Is It? — compliment → reverence → homage

compliment vs. homage

compliment vs. homage: A compliment is smaller and more casual than homage — a compliment is a brief kind remark, while homage is a deliberate, often public tribute meant to honor someone's whole legacy.

reverence vs. homage

reverence vs. homage: Reverence can feel even deeper than homage: homage is usually a specific act of tribute, but reverence describes an ongoing, deep-seated feeling of awe and respect.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — hom-/hum-

root — hom-/hum-: man, human being (Latin (homo))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin homo meant 'man, human being.' In medieval Old French, homage originally described the formal ceremony where a vassal publicly declared himself the 'man' (loyal servant) of his lord. Today, paying homage still means publicly, formally honoring someone.

Use the root in a new word: human

Use the root in a new word: human: Every human being deserves to be treated with basic dignity and respect.
